chapters.summary: Nehemiah hears that the wall of Jerusalem lies broken down and its people are in great distress; he weeps, fasts, and prays, asking God to remember his promises and confessing the sin of Israel.
keyPoints: In Shushan, Nehemiah hears from his brothers a report of Jerusalem's distress, and he sits down and weeps, mourning for many days.
He fasts and prays before God, confessing the sins of Israel, including his own father's house, and asks God to remember the covenant he made.
Nehemiah asks God to grant him success and favor before the king, preparing the way for the opportunity to rebuild the wall.
chapters.application: When we see brokenness in the church or in society, let us follow Nehemiah's example: first come before God in prayer and fasting, confess our own shortcomings, ask him to open the way, and then act to repair what is broken.

chapters.summary: After praying before the king of Persia, Nehemiah is granted permission to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the wall, and he encourages the people to rise up and build.
keyPoints: As the king's cupbearer, Nehemiah's face shows the sorrow he feels over Jerusalem, and the king asks him the reason.
After praying, Nehemiah asks the king for permission to return to Judah and rebuild the wall; the king grants his request and provides letters and timber.
By night Nehemiah surveys the wall, then encourages the people to rise up and build, refuting the mockery of Sanballat and the others.
chapters.application: When we face difficulties, let us first pray, asking God to open the way, and then take action. God moves hearts and provides resources so that we can accomplish his will.

chapters.summary: Nehemiah chapter 3 records in detail the rebuilding of each section of Jerusalem's wall, accomplished through the cooperative labor of many different families and groups.
keyPoints: The priests take the lead in rebuilding the Sheep Gate and consecrate it, setting a spiritual example for the rest.
People from every walk of life take part eagerly, including goldsmiths and merchants, showing the unity of the whole community.
Some nobles refuse to take part, but most of the people labor diligently, and the entire project is completed.
chapters.application: In the church or community, each of us has different gifts; let us gladly take part in the work of building up, never despising a small role. Working together with one heart, we can surely accomplish the mission God has entrusted to us.

chapters.summary: Nehemiah leads the people in rebuilding the wall; facing the mockery and threats of their enemies, they pray and keep on working, and the project is finally completed.
keyPoints: Their enemies Sanballat and Tobiah mock them and plot to attack, so Nehemiah prays, asking God to strengthen the people.
Under Nehemiah's leadership the people work with one hand and hold a weapon with the other, standing together against their enemies.
Nehemiah encourages the people to remember the great and awesome Lord and to fight for their families and the wall, and in the end the wall is finished.
chapters.application: When we face opposition and pressure, let us follow Nehemiah's example: pray first, asking God for help, while continuing faithfully to carry out our responsibilities, trusting that God will surely watch over us.

chapters.summary: Nehemiah rebukes the nobles and officials for lending at interest, demands that they restore the people's fields and repayments, and has them swear an oath to keep their word.
keyPoints: Because of the shortage of grain and the burden of the king's tax, the people borrow money, mortgaging their fields and houses, and some are even forced to sell their children into slavery.
Nehemiah is greatly angered and rebukes the nobles and officials, demanding that they stop charging interest and restore everything they have taken.
The people swear an oath to do as he says, Nehemiah exhorts them by his own example, and the people are blessed.
chapters.application: When our own interests are at stake, let us follow Nehemiah's example: caring for the weak, refusing to exploit others, and putting love and justice into action.

chapters.summary: Facing the schemes of his enemies and the threats of a false prophet, Nehemiah stands firm in reliance on God and completes the rebuilding of the wall.
keyPoints: His enemies invite Nehemiah to meet with them four times, intending to harm him, but he refuses and sees through their scheme.
Sanballat sends an open letter spreading false rumors, but Nehemiah denies them and prays, asking God to strengthen his hands.
The false prophet Shemaiah tries to lure Nehemiah into hiding in the temple, but Nehemiah sees through the trap, refuses, and presses on to finish the work.
chapters.application: When we face attacks and rumors, let us follow Nehemiah's example: stay watchful in prayer, hold our ground, and not shrink back out of fear — God will surely strengthen the work of our hands.

chapters.summary: Nehemiah chapter 7 records how, after the wall is finished, Nehemiah appoints men to oversee the city and reviews the genealogical records of the people, to confirm the pure identity of those who have returned.
keyPoints: With the wall finished, Nehemiah appoints men to oversee Jerusalem, instructing that the gates be opened and shut only at the proper times.
Moved by God, Nehemiah gathers the people together to register their genealogies and verify the identity of those who have returned.
The registration shows that the returned community numbers forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty, besides their male and female servants and the singers.
chapters.application: Let us value our spiritual heritage, be assured of our identity within God's household, and do our part to uphold order within the community, serving with a thankful heart.

chapters.summary: The people of Israel gather to listen to Ezra read the Law, and after coming to understand it, they rejoice and keep the Feast of Tabernacles.
keyPoints: The people gather as one man at the Water Gate and ask Ezra to bring out the Book of the Law and read it.
Ezra blesses the LORD, and all the people lift up their hands, answer 'Amen, Amen,' and bow down to worship.
The Levites explain the Law so the people can understand it, and when the people grasp its meaning they weep, but are urged instead to rejoice.
chapters.application: When we read God's word and come to understand his heart, sorrow turns to joy. Let us delight always in God's word and share that joy with others, for the joy of the LORD is our strength.

chapters.summary: The people of Israel fast and confess their sins; the Levites lead them in recounting God's grace and mercy from the creation onward, and the people make a covenant, swearing to keep the Law.
keyPoints: The people gather to fast, wearing sackcloth and putting dust on their heads; they separate themselves from all foreigners and confess their own sins and the sins of their ancestors.
The Levites recount at length God's grace in creation, in choosing Abraham, in the exodus from Egypt, in guiding them through the wilderness, in giving the Law, and in bringing them into Canaan.

The people acknowledge God's justice and mercy — that though they were disciplined for their rebellion, God in his grace still preserved them — and so they set their seal to a covenant, swearing to keep the Law.
chapters.application: Let us regularly examine our own hearts, remember God's grace throughout history and in our own lives, and respond to his faithfulness with repentance and obedience, renewing our resolve to keep his word.

chapters.summary: Nehemiah chapter 10 records how the people of Israel set their seal to a covenant before God, pledging to keep the Law — including not intermarrying with foreigners, keeping the Sabbath, and giving the firstfruits and the tithe.
keyPoints: Led by Nehemiah and the priests, the people sign a sealed document, pledging their willingness to keep God's Law.
The terms of the covenant include not intermarrying with foreigners, keeping the Sabbath and the sabbatical year, and forgiving debts.
The people pledge to bring offerings for the temple — firstfruits, firstborn, and tithes among them — to support the service of the Levites and priests.
chapters.application: Though we today are not bound to keep the letter of the old covenant's regulations, we should follow the example of the Israelites, obeying God with a covenant-keeping heart, remaining faithful in giving and service, and living out a testimony of our faith.

chapters.summary: Nehemiah chapter 11 records how some of the people of Israel volunteer to live in Jerusalem, how the leaders and the rest of the people cast lots to choose who would settle in the holy city, and it lists the names of those who lived there.
keyPoints: The people pray for the holy city, and some volunteer to live in Jerusalem; of the rest, lots are cast so that one out of every ten comes to live there.
The leaders and those who freely offer themselves settle in the holy city, and lists are given for both the tribe of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin.
The Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and other temple servants also live in Jerusalem, sustaining the ongoing worship there.
chapters.application: Let us gladly commit ourselves to God's household; even when it costs us something, may we be willing to give ourselves for the church and the kingdom of God, so that worship and service may continue.

chapters.summary: Nehemiah chapter 12 records the lists of priests and Levites and describes the grand dedication ceremony of the wall, displaying the gratitude and worship of the people of Israel toward God.
keyPoints: It records the names of the priests and Levites who returned together with Zerubbabel.
It describes how, in Nehemiah's time, the priests and Levites served in their divisions and oversaw the storerooms of the temple.
At the dedication of the wall, two great processions of thanksgiving walk around the city, offering thanks and praise to God.
chapters.application: Let us keep a thankful heart in our daily life and work, offering worship and praise to God as a sacrifice, and faithfully carrying out the duties he has entrusted to us.

chapters.summary: Nehemiah chapter 13 records how, after returning to Jerusalem once more, Nehemiah cleanses the temple, sets the duties of the priests and Levites in order, and corrects the people's violations of the Law.
keyPoints: Nehemiah discovers that Tobiah has taken over a room in the temple storerooms, so he throws out all his household furniture and cleanses the room.
Because the Levites have received no support, they have fled to their fields; Nehemiah restores the practice of the tithe, bringing the Levites back to their posts.
Nehemiah rebukes those who conduct business on the Sabbath and forbids intermarriage with foreigners, reaffirming the Law.
chapters.application: When we drift from the right path in our lives, let us, like Nehemiah, have the courage to correct what is wrong, return to God's Law, and hold fast to a holy life.
